account:
There seems to be some coordinated activity among the local tradespeople, but I have not established its full purpose. Townsfolk repeatedly reported a 'bridge or port change' discussed at the bakery, naming the baker, builder, innkeeper, freight and neighbour in different combinations. Yesterday I saw the builder give the baker oak planks and a lantern. Those could be ordinary supplies or materials for arrangements; I cannot tell which. Today the innkeeper said he was arranging an inn bread order and wanted to find the baker or freight. He said he had not seen a bridge or port proposal. The neighbour said the baker and freight had recently been at the bakery and that the baker had fresh bread to deliver, but offered no reliable direction.

The clearest unusual arrangement is tonight's civic presentation in the town hall great hall, from 18:00 to 18:30. The signed appointment supplement says it honours municipal public service, is organised by the inn and local tradespeople, and was approved by me yesterday. I know that approval from the written record. It specifically asks me to arrive at 18:00, not earlier, so organisers can finish preparations around their work. I also heard the secretary say she would keep the presentation's contents private. My best guess is that at least some of this quiet coordination concerns a surprise appreciation event, possibly with bread and decorations. That remains a guess, not proof that the bakery rumours are connected.

There is also genuine riverside business: freight recommended lights at both ferry landings and clearly marked waiting areas, and I asked the secretary to record those suggestions. That does not establish a larger bridge or port scheme. I attended the morning mill inspection and saw 76 hay bales in its stock chest; I have not received a detailed supply report. I am now home ahead of noon lunch, with council letters at 13:00, tea with the neighbour at 15:00, office at 16:30, and the presentation at exactly 18:00 still to keep.
